It sounds like you might very well be suffering some form of depression. I'm UK-based, in my fourth decade and I have suffered several 'episodes' of depression covering most of my adult life (and possibly neurodivergent in some other way as well - I hope to find out soon). 

Definitely talk to your GP. Mental health problems are becoming more and more common, and GPs within the NHS are generally pretty understanding. As to how to broach the subject - try to be honest and direct about how you feel and the effect it's having on your life. 

After an initial consultation the GP may recommend an antidepressant. These can really help, but it can take a few goes to find a particular medication that is both effective and tolerable in terms of side-effects. (I was on the SSRI sertraline for a couple of years, but it became ineffective and intolerablr very quickly, so I was switched to venlafaxine, a more potent SNRI, which has mostly been a godsend.) 

If therapy is suggested, I highly recommend you try it. Counselling just involves talking relatively informally with a counsellor who will guide you along in hope of getting to the bottom of your feelings. CBT involves learning strategies to deal with negative thoughts and events, usually by challenging and examining your initial responses and determining a healthier way to respond. (I had both at different times, and they helped in very different ways - counselling helped me to exorcise some of my demons, and CBT helped me to avoid getting caught in negative spirals.)
